title: Daily standup alternatives: 7 ways to stay aligned without the meeting
summary: Seven alternatives to the daily standup, from async updates to AI meeting assistants, what research says about each and what you lose.
body_markdown:
In June 2025, Microsoft’s[Work Trend Index recommended](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/breaking-down-infinite-workday) something that would have sounded odd a few years earlier: hand “status meetings, routine reports, admin churn” to AI and agents, and keep people’s time for the work that needs them. The daily standup is the most common status meeting there is.


Teams are not only replacing standups because of AI. They are doing it because the calendar is full. This guide covers seven alternatives to the daily standup, what each is good for, how AI meeting assistants compare with async standups, and what the research says you lose when the meeting goes away.


---


## Why teams are looking for alternatives in 2026


The pressure comes from the cost of interruption. Microsoft’s 2025 telemetry shows workers are interrupted every two minutes during core hours, 48% of employees describe their work as chaotic and fragmented, and meetings after 8 p.m. grew 16% year over year.[A 2026 study of software practitioners](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ESEM.2026.7) found that 76.4% feel less productive on high-meeting days.


Cutting meetings appears to help.[Laker and colleagues](https://sloanreview.mit.edu/article/the-surprising-impact-of-meeting-free-days/) surveyed 76 companies, each with more than 1,000 employees, that introduced between one and five meeting-free days a week. Employees reported more autonomy and cooperation and less stress, with the best results at three meeting-free days. The data comes from pulse surveys without a control group, but the direction is consistent with what teams tell us.


The goal of an alternative is the same as the standup’s: shared awareness, a plan for the day and blockers raised early. Only the format changes.


---


## Seven alternatives to the daily standup


Alternative How it works Best for Main risk


1. Async written standup Everyone answers the standup questions in chat at the start of their day Remote and multi-time-zone teams Updates turn into copy-paste if nobody reads them


2. Fewer live standups Meet three or four times a week instead of five Teams that communicate well already Gaps on the days you skip


3. Board walk The team updates the task board; the lead reviews changes Teams with a well-kept board Context and blockers do not fit in a ticket


4. End-of-day update A short written note of what got done and what is next Teams with flexible hours Problems surface a day later


5. Hybrid Async updates daily, one live sync a week Most distributed teams The weekly call grows into a long meeting


6. AI meeting assistant An assistant records and summarizes the meetings you keep Teams that keep a live standup Still requires everyone in the meeting


7. Automated status reports Updates are compiled from check-ins, tools and agents into one report Teams with humans and AI agents doing the work Missing the human context behind the data


Option 2 has direct research support. After observing 102 standups in 15 teams,[Stray, Moe and Sjøberg](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.07650) suggested teams “stop meeting daily if 3-4 times a week is sufficient”.


Seven alternatives placed by live time required and context captured. The positions are our assessment, not measured data.


---


## AI meeting assistants vs async standups


The two are often confused, but they solve different problems.


An **AI meeting assistant** joins a call, transcribes it and produces a summary and action items. It makes a meeting you keep cheaper to follow up on. It does not remove the meeting: everyone still has to be there at the same time.


An **async standup** removes the meeting. Each person writes a short update when their day starts, and the team reads a combined report. Nothing needs a shared time slot.


AI meeting assistant Async standup


Removes the meeting No Yes


Works across time zones Only if everyone can join Yes


Captures blockers If someone says them out loud In a dedicated question


Best when The live conversation is the point Coordination is the point


Our rule of thumb: if the standup is mostly status, you need no meeting, not a meeting bot. If the standup is mostly a real conversation, keep the meeting and use an assistant for the notes.


---


## What you lose without a live meeting


The strongest counterpoint comes from[a study of 61,182 Microsoft employees](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-021-01196-4) during the first six months of 2020. When the company went fully remote, synchronous communication dropped, asynchronous communication rose and collaboration networks became “more static and siloed,” with fewer bridges between groups. The study covered remote work in general, but the warning applies to any team that turns every interaction into writing.


The 2025 standup research adds a second risk.[Rietze and Zacher](https://doi.org/10.1080/1359432X.2025.2508178) found the standup’s value runs through psychological safety, the sense that it is safe to speak up in the team. Some of that comes from seeing each other regularly. An alternative that removes all shared time can remove that too.


That is why we rarely recommend options 3, 4 or 7 alone. Pair them with some live time, even a short weekly call.


---


## How to choose an alternative


Start from the problem your current standup has.


- **It runs long or has too many people:** split it, or move updates to writing (options 1 and 5). See[how long a daily standup should be](https://www.dailybot.com/blog/how-long-should-a-daily-standup-be/) .
- **It does not fit your time zones:** async or hybrid (options 1 and 5). See[standups across time zones](https://www.dailybot.com/blog/standups-across-time-zones/) .
- **It feels like a report to the boss:** fix the purpose before replacing it. See[are daily standups worth it](https://www.dailybot.com/blog/are-daily-standups-worth-it/) .
- **AI agents are doing part of the work:** automated status reports (option 7), so humans and agents show up in the same place.

## Frequently asked questions


**What can I use instead of a daily standup?** Async written updates, fewer live standups, board walks, end-of-day notes, a hybrid of async and weekly calls, AI meeting assistants or automated status reports.


**Is an async standup better than a meeting?** For distributed teams and status-heavy standups, usually. For close collaboration or incidents, a live conversation is faster.


**Do AI meeting assistants replace standups?** No. They summarize meetings you keep. To remove the meeting, use an async standup.


**What do you lose by dropping the standup?** Some cross-team connection and some of the safety to raise problems. Keep a short weekly live call to protect both.


**How do I know if my team needs a daily meeting?** If most updates are status and most people do not need to react to them, you do not need a daily meeting.
